# `unreleased-allocation`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a mechanically identified allocation with no visible matching release or
ownership return before scope exit.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Repeated execution leaks memory; an `errdefer`-only cleanup still leaks on
successful returns.

## When it fires

The rule also reports a failed `realloc` path that returns a newly allocated
replacement without releasing the still-valid original allocation.

It tracks simple allocator bindings across local blocks, `if`/`else` branches,
exhaustive `switch` branches, `while` and `for` loops, loop `else` branches,
early returns, ownership returns, and propagated errors covered by `errdefer`.
Local binding and aggregate moves are followed until the destination is released
or transferred. Direct calls to resolvable helpers are followed when the
matching parameter is provably only borrowed or unconditionally released before
any visible exit; indirect calls, optional captures, reallocations, cross-nested
labeled exits, and other ambiguous constructs retain the conservative lexical
analysis. Allocator fields and function parameters declared under the
`contracts.arena-allocators` project setting inherit the surrounding arena
lifetime and do not require individual releases. Functions documenting that
their allocator should be an arena provide the same lifetime proof, including
for private helpers that receive that parameter.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

pub fn run(gpa: std.mem.Allocator) !void {
    const buf = try gpa.alloc(u8, 16);
    buf[0] = 1;
}
```
